solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slender, small, and easy to lift

parts.note: something light weighs little, so it is easy to pick up

explanation.surface: A description of some neat object: thin, compact and no trouble to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads as three adjectives for one thing, but only the first is the definition; the other two build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight and slender are synonyms for a thin, delicate build.

clue.text: British money's sound in Scottish city

indicators.note: sound here means the word heard, not spelt, matches the city

parts.note: sterling is the currency of the UK

explanation.surface: The pound is in good health in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound reads as healthy; it signals a word that is spoken alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling is a city in central Scotland, famous for its castle.

clue.text: I had taken over island, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
the Isle of Man, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an island seized, as a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression or turn of phrase whose sense isn't literal.

clue.text: After red card, chaps, lacking leader? Cheer up

indicators.note: after means the chaps follow the card

parts.note: hearts is a red suit in playing cards

indicators.note: lacking leader drops the opening letter of the word for chaps

parts.note: men is a plain synonym for chaps

explanation.surface: A football team down to fewer men after their captain is sent off, told to keep their spirits up.
explanation.walkthrough: Red card suggests a sending-off in football; here it is a card from a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them, raising their spirits.

clue.text: Social group cleric converted

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of cleric are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of cleric are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A churchman has changed faith and joined a new set of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: With a cleric in view, converted suggests religion; here it only reorders letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a set of people sharing interests or company, as in a social circle.

clue.text: It's better coming from him, proverbially

indicators.note: coming from means the answer emerges from inside the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of him and the start of proverbially

explanation.surface: A saying that sounds wiser when spoken by a certain man.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to make it superior, which is to enhance it.

clue.text: Select group of MPs, perhaps, to pledge support for ball

parts.note: to commit is to promise or bind oneself
a golf ball is placed on a tee

explanation.surface: Parliamentarians vowing to back a grand social event.
explanation.walkthrough: Select reads as an adjective in the political sense, and a select committee is a Commons panel; ball suggests a dance, but it is a golf ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A select committee is a panel of MPs that scrutinises a particular area of government.

clue.text: Cake Alice demolished, getting taller, ultimately

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so these letters are reconstructed

parts.note: the five letters of the name are the fodder

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of taller

parts.note: only the last letter of taller is used

explanation.surface: Alice eats cake in Wonderland and grows taller.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Alice in Wonderland, where eating a cake makes her grow.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry, filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Activist set on fire area in plant

indicators.note: in means the burning and area go inside the plant

parts.note: mint is a herb
lit is the past tense of light, to set burning

explanation.surface: A protester torched part of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant reads as a factory, but it is the herb mint.
explanation.definitionFit: A militant is a campaigner who takes forceful, combative action for a cause.

clue.text: Unusually intense blow resulting in problem for person serving

indicators.note: unusually means in an irregular way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A heavy knock leaves a waiter or player in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Person serving suggests a waiter; it is a tennis server.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis elbow is a painful strain of forearm tendons, common among racket players who serve.

clue.text: Hint on page spotted?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it

parts.note: to imply is to suggest without saying outright

explanation.surface: A question whether a clue has been noticed on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted looks like noticed; it means covered in spots, and the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimply face is covered with spots, so pimply describes skin that is spotty.

clue.text: Learner in academic stream is secretive type

indicators.note: in tells you the learner goes inside the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge, the university town

explanation.surface: A student in a university stream who keeps everything to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Stream suggests an ability set at school, but it is a river. The Cam flows through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who clams up refuses to talk, so a clam is a close, uncommunicative person.

clue.text: Look after leg — it's 9 Down, say

parts.note: to tend is to care for
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
taken as the two words it is

explanation.surface: Advice to care for an injured limb, since the problem is a familiar sports injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are cricket synonyms: the leg side of the field is the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis elbow is an example of tendon inflammation, hence say.

clue.text: Not flexible at home, passing around front of goal

indicators.note: around means the brief word wraps the goal's first letter

parts.note: passing as in fleeting, short-lived

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of goal

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A rigid footballer stays at home, passing the ball around near the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Passing suggests football with goal nearby, but it means fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent describes someone who refuses to compromise, which is to be unbending.

clue.text: Prompt to include article that's left

indicators.note: to include means the reminder contains the article

parts.note: a reminder is a prompt to memory

explanation.surface: An editor's note to put in the piece that was omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what stays behind after the rest is taken away.

clue.text: Large number in bar, e.g., I'm entertaining

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs through the end of bar, all of e.g. and I'm, and the start of entertaining

explanation.surface: A barman boasts of hosting a crowd at his pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Entertaining looks like a containment signal, but it is simply part of the text holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment can mean any great crowd, by extension from the military unit.

clue.text: Best work in epic art seems different

indicators.note: different suggests a changed form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: these three words supply the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A critic notes that epic paintings look unlike the rest of an artist's output.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is an artist's finest achievement, the pinnacle of their output.

clue.text: Hard diamonds cut

parts.note: severe as in harsh or tough

explanation.surface: Tough gemstones that have been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Severed means cut off or sliced through, as a limb or tie is.

clue.text: Thwart gathering arranged to promote business?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the work of promoting a firm
an event is an organised gathering

explanation.surface: Someone blocks a meeting that was set up for marketing.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening, which is to thwart it.

clue.text: Last month, in short, a politician beat it

parts.note: December is the year's final month, shortened
taken as written

explanation.surface: An MP was defeated at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: Beat it reads as defeated; it is slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, the same as the slang order to clear off.

clue.text: Have responsibility about Eastern vase, initially, holding water?

indicators.note: about means the responsible phrase surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to be liable is to be responsible

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of vase

parts.note: the vase supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of an Oriental vase that may or may not hold water.
explanation.walkthrough: Holding water reads literally with the vase; an argument that holds water is sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that holds water is credible, convincing enough to be accepted.

clue.text: Business at home in American quarter, for example

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A firm working from home in a district of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarter reads as a district; it is the 25-cent piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The US quarter is a twenty-five-cent piece of currency, an example of a coin.

clue.text: Take care of leading man with a hot drink

parts.note: c/o, care of, used in addresses
a commanding officer leads the men
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse looks after a film star with a warm beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading man suggests an actor; it is a commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a warm chocolate beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Large snake — it goes the other way on board

definitions.text: it goes the other way on board

parts.note: the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: A big serpent heading the opposite direction across a game board.
explanation.walkthrough: In Snakes and Ladders, snakes take a counter down and ladders take it up.
explanation.definitionFit: On a Snakes and Ladders board a ladder moves you up, opposite to a snake's slide.

clue.text: Young women holding right tools for plumbers

indicators.note: holding means the women contain the letter for right

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Young women apprentices carrying the correct plumbing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrenches are spanners used to grip and turn pipes and nuts, standard plumbing equipment.

clue.text: Make a mockery of staff dividing earnings

indicators.note: dividing means the staff splits the earnings word in two

parts.note: pay is money earned
a rod is a stick or staff

explanation.surface: Ridiculing the workers by splitting their wages.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff reads as employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody something is to imitate it mockingly, sending it up.

clue.text: World record time shortened, finally

parts.note: an atlas is a book recording the world's geography
time shortened to its abbreviation, a single letter

explanation.surface: An athlete's world-best time has been cut, after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: World record looks like an athletics feat; it is a book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: At last expresses that something has happened eventually, after a long delay.
